title: Career Roadmap: Financial Analyst
summary: A Financial Analyst evaluates financial information, business performance, market trends and investment opportunities to help organisations make informed financial decisions. Analysts prepare financial models, budgets, forecasts, reports and recommendations for management, investors or clients.

blocks.text: A Financial Analyst evaluates financial information, business performance, market trends and investment opportunities to help organisations make informed financial decisions. Analysts prepare financial models, budgets, forecasts, reports and recommendations for management, investors or clients.

A BS in Economics or Finance provides a relevant foundation in economic theory, financial markets, quantitative analysis and business decision-making. Practical skills in spreadsheets, accounting, financial modelling and data analysis help graduates prepare for entry-level roles.

blocks.text: A financial analyst role is distinct from regulated investment advisory, securities research or other licensed activities. Specific responsibilities may require additional qualifications, registrations or regulatory compliance, depending on the jurisdiction and employer.

This is a suggested progression, not the official semester structure of the degree. Adjust it to the actual programme duration and curriculum.
Stage 1 — Economics, accounting and quantitative foundations

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: First year
Learn

items.text: Microeconomics and macroeconomics.

blocks.label: Financial accounting
blocks.text: assets, liabilities, equity, revenue and expenses.

items.text: Income statements, balance sheets and cash flow statements.
Business mathematics, percentages, ratios and time value of money.
Probability, descriptive statistics and introductory econometrics.

blocks.label: Excel fundamentals
blocks.text: formulas, lookups, charts and pivot tables.

items.text: Business writing and presentation skills.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Analyse the financial statements of a publicly listed company.
Calculate profitability, liquidity and leverage ratios.
Build an Excel workbook that summarises revenue and expenses.
Explain how inflation, interest rates and economic growth can affect businesses.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Understand the relationship between financial statements, business performance and economic conditions.
Stage 2 — Corporate finance and financial modelling

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Second year
Learn

items.text: Time value of money, discounting and compounding.
Cost of capital and the fundamentals of capital budgeting.
Financial ratio analysis and trend analysis.
Budgeting, forecasting and variance analysis.
Net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR) and payback period.
Excel functions, scenario analysis and sensitivity analysis.
Financial markets, bonds, equities and interest-rate fundamentals.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Build a three-year revenue and expense forecast.
Compare actual financial results against a budget.
Calculate NPV and IRR for a hypothetical investment.
Create best-case, base-case and worst-case scenarios.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Build spreadsheet models that support business and financial decisions.
Stage 3 — Valuation, research and data analysis

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Third year
Learn

items.text: Discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation fundamentals.
Comparable-company analysis and financial benchmarking.
Forecast assumptions, terminal value and valuation sensitivity.
Advanced Excel, Power Query and financial data organisation.
SQL for extracting and analysing financial information.
Power BI or Tableau for financial reporting.
Python fundamentals for automation and financial data analysis.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Prepare a simplified valuation model for a listed company.
Compare financial performance across companies in one industry.
Build a dashboard showing revenue, margins, costs and cash flow.
Write a short analytical report explaining risks and assumptions.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Combine financial modelling, data analysis and business interpretation in a coherent report.

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Final learning phase
Learn

items.text: Advanced financial modelling and forecasting.
Financial planning and analysis (FP&A) workflows.
Investment research or corporate finance, depending on your chosen track.
Financial risk, scenario planning and sensitivity analysis.
Data quality, model checks and version control.
Business communication, executive summaries and presentations.
Relevant financial reporting and regulatory concepts for the target role.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Complete a full financial analysis project.
Prepare a forecast, valuation or budget model with documented assumptions.
Seek a finance internship or supervised analytical project.
Practise financial modelling tests and interview questions.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Present a defensible financial analysis with clear assumptions, risks and recommendations.

blocks.text: Learn Excel and financial statement analysis first. Python and SQL become more valuable as the volume and complexity of financial data increase.
Use public financial disclosures or clearly labelled hypothetical data. Avoid presenting educational models as professional investment advice.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Financial statement analysis

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Beginner

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Analyse three years of financial statements for a publicly listed company.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Revenue growth, gross and operating margins, liquidity, leverage, profitability and cash flow trends.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Excel workbook, ratio table, charts and a concise financial performance report.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Budgeting and forecasting model

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Create a financial model for a hypothetical company with revenue, costs, operating expenses and cash flow.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Monthly budgeting, actual-versus-budget analysis, assumptions, scenario planning and forecast accuracy checks.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Spreadsheet model, forecast dashboard and management summary.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Company valuation model

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate to advanced

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Create a simplified discounted cash flow valuation using public company disclosures and explicitly documented assumptions.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Revenue and margin forecasts, free cash flow, discounting, terminal value and sensitivity analysis.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Valuation workbook, assumptions sheet, sensitivity table and risk discussion.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Financial performance dashboard

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Advanced

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Create an interactive Power BI dashboard using public or simulated company financial data.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: KPI definitions, period comparisons, revenue trends, margin analysis, cost breakdown and data refresh processes.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Dashboard, source-data notes, metric definitions and an executive briefing.

For each project, document the data source, period covered, formulas, assumptions, limitations and quality checks. Distinguish reported figures from your own estimates, and do not fabricate financial data.
Begin applying when you can interpret financial statements, use Excel confidently and explain at least one financial model you have built.

Stage 1 — Finance Intern or Junior Financial Analyst
Prepare reports, maintain models, validate figures and support routine analysis.
Stage 2 — Financial Analyst
Own forecasts, financial models, variance analysis and defined business or investment analyses.
Stage 3 — Senior Analyst or Finance Specialist
Lead complex modelling, provide decision support and specialise in FP&A, valuation or risk.
Stage 4 — Finance Manager, FP&A Manager or Research Lead
Lead financial planning, analytical teams, business partnering or specialist research functions.
Progression depends on analytical quality, business impact, communication, sector knowledge and opportunities—not years of experience alone.

Financial Analyst readiness
0 of 12
Understand income statements, balance sheets and cash flow statements
Calculate key profitability, liquidity and leverage ratios
Use Excel formulas, lookups, pivot tables and financial modelling
Understand time value of money, NPV and IRR
Build a budget and financial forecast with documented assumptions
Perform scenario and sensitivity analysis
Understand DCF and comparable-company valuation fundamentals
Use SQL or Python for basic financial data analysis
Create a financial dashboard or clear analytical report
Explain model limitations, data sources and key financial risks
Complete at least two documented finance portfolio projects
Prepare for accounting, valuation, Excel and business case interviews
A job-ready graduate should be able to:

items.text: Interpret financial statements and identify business performance trends.
Build spreadsheet-based financial models and forecasts.
Calculate financial ratios and evaluate assumptions.
Understand valuation methods and their limitations.
Analyse data using Excel and, where useful, SQL or Python.
Communicate findings through clear reports and dashboards.
Identify financial risks and explain alternative scenarios.
Demonstrate accuracy, ethical judgement and attention to detail.
Present practical work through a portfolio and technical interviews.

blocks.label: Recommended priority
blocks.text: Master accounting fundamentals and Excel first, then learn financial modelling, forecasting and valuation. Add Power BI, SQL and Python to strengthen data analysis. Build a portfolio with a financial statement analysis, a budget forecast and a company valuation model to demonstrate practical readiness for entry-level finance roles.
